meta.columns_note: all columns of public.sites except id, notes and created_at; id here is a build key (slug plus body), not the database id
meta.label: Sites from the Supabase edit store (loaded from a teammate-supplied CSV): known sites and candidates. Descriptive list, not scored results.
limits: Sites are places named as analogs in a teammate-supplied list. They are not scored results.
Coordinates come from a teammate-supplied CSV; many are approximate.
The CSV gave no source links, so none are shown and no site has passed a sources check.
All descriptive text (why it is an analog, where the analogy breaks, experiments) is teammate-written and unreviewed.
Candidate rows are suggestions only. They are not in our reference list.
The v1 used flag is a coordinate match against the v1 site list, not a name match.
Earth sites differ from the Moon and Mars in gravity, air, radiation and dust; see the ledger.
meta.list_note: known sites are our reference list; candidate rows are teammate suggestions, not in our reference list, and are not used for distances or the region drop rule
meta.v1_used_rule: true: within the v1 site match radius of a v1 site run for the same body. null (unknown): near a v1 site but not matching, or v1 ran that site for the other body only. false: farther than the v1 exclusion distance from every v1 site.

sites.experiments_done: Mars analog field research; Paralana radioactive hot springs as a habitability analog; field-geology training.
sites.experiments_possible: Biosignatures in hydrothermal deposits; radiation-tolerant microbiology; rover tests on rocky slopes.
sites.how_to_modify: Cleared test pads; basaltic simulant overlays; fenced plots at Paralana springs for clean sampling.
sites.key_differences: Vegetation; thick air; Precambrian rocks not basaltic.
sites.name: Arkaroola (Mars-Oz)
sites.why_analog: Southern-hemisphere Mars analog with hydrothermal springs.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo crews trained on barren basaltic terrain and pumice; later planetary field studies (Mars and Moon).
sites.experiments_possible: Barren-basalt EVA traverses; cold-weather equipment; dust and sand transport; rover tests on unvegetated volcanic sand plains.
sites.how_to_modify: Summer ops with simulant overlays; use the 2 km window that excludes lakes.
sites.key_differences: Wet, glacial; mid-high latitude light but not lunar polar; Earth atmosphere.
sites.name: Askja caldera
sites.why_analog: Apollo training landscape: barren, cold basalt.

sites.experiments_done: Carnegie Mellon's Nomad rover completed a ~200 km teleoperated traverse in 1997 to rehearse lunar exploration, testing panoramic telepresence, autonomous navigation and solar power.
sites.experiments_possible: Long-range autonomous lunar-rover traverses with telepresence; solar-power and battery cycling under clear skies; dust accumulation on optics and panels; navigation over featureless gravel plains.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant lanes and blasted crater mock-ups; low-sun dawn/dusk operations; dust-loading tests on solar panels.
sites.key_differences: Air, wind; mid-latitude sun; andesitic gravels.
sites.name: Atacama Desert (CMU Nomad rover traverse)
sites.why_analog: First long-distance robotic lunar-rover rehearsal.

sites.experiments_done: Viking-type labelled-release and pyrolysis experiments repeated on near-sterile soils; Life in the Atacama rover (2003-05); ARADS 1 m rover-drill campaigns (2016-19); perchlorate/nitrate oxidant chemistry; studies of the dry limit of life.
sites.experiments_possible: Mars Sample Return caching and sample-triage rehearsal; detection of organics protected below the oxidised layer (1-2 m drilling); dust and UV sensor calibration; autonomous science-target selection by rover.
sites.how_to_modify: UV-sterilise test plots; spike soils to Mars perchlorate levels (0.5-1 wt%); overlay basaltic Mars simulant (MGS-1) for wheel and drill tests.
sites.key_differences: Andesitic alluvium not basalt; thick atmosphere shields UV; still ~10^5-10^6 cells per gram.
sites.name: Atacama Desert - Yungay core
sites.why_analog: Driest non-polar desert; default analog for Mars soil chemistry and life detection.

sites.experiments_done: Driest soils measured on Earth (Azua-Bustos et al. 2017): very low water activity, minimal microbial life; Mars soil-habitability comparisons.
sites.experiments_possible: Life-detection instrument limits of detection; perchlorate and nitrate oxidant chemistry; rover drill tests below oxidised layer.
sites.how_to_modify: Perchlorate-spiked plots; UV-sterilised strips; basaltic simulant overlays for rover tests.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; nitrate-mining history; still not sterile.
sites.name: Atacama - Maria Elena South
sites.why_analog: Reference for the driest soils on Earth and Mars habitability limits.

sites.experiments_done: Microbial life in sub-zero brines; methane seeps; sulfate and chloride precipitates in permafrost.
sites.experiments_possible: Methane detection and isotope tests (Curiosity/TGO-like); sulfate spectroscopy; brine-permafrost interaction studies.
sites.how_to_modify: Enclosed spring outlets to study freezing under reduced pressure.
sites.key_differences: Thick atmosphere; life abundant at springs; polar light.
sites.name: Axel Heiberg - Gypsum Hill and Lost Hammer springs
sites.why_analog: Unique analog for possible Martian subsurface brines and methane.

sites.experiments_done: Jarosite type locality used for spectral and mineralogical comparisons with Meridiani jarosite found by Opportunity.
sites.experiments_possible: Sulfate spectroscopy; jarosite stability and alteration rates; Mossbauer reference spectra.
sites.how_to_modify: Spoil-heap test plots; dry-season sampling.
sites.key_differences: Coastal Mediterranean; mining spoils; vegetation.
sites.name: Barranco del Jaroso (Sierra Almagrera)
sites.why_analog: Reference site for jarosite (type locality).

sites.experiments_done: Buried-ice dating and dry-permafrost studies; polygon mapping compared with Phoenix landing site; vapour-diffusion and sublimation measurements; ice-drill tests.
sites.experiments_possible: Ground-ice drilling to 1 m (rehearsal for Arcadia Planitia ice targets); thermal-model validation; polygon trenching; cold-tolerant robotics and power.
sites.how_to_modify: Lay Mars simulant over ice-cemented ground; CO2-purged tents to run sublimation at lower humidity.
sites.key_differences: Dolerite/sandstone, not Martian basalt; polar sun regime differs from mid-latitude Mars targets; thick air.
sites.name: Beacon Valley and University Valley (Dry Valleys)
sites.why_analog: Best Earth analog for Martian dry permafrost and buried ice.

sites.experiments_done: Desert RATS 2008-2011: Space Exploration Vehicle (pressurised rover) multi-day traverses, two-crew EVA protocols, communication-latency trials and science-team backroom operations.
sites.experiments_possible: Long-duration traverse rehearsal for the Artemis pressurised rover; dust-ingress tests on hatches; autonomous rover navigation; teleoperation with 2.6 s round-trip delay.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant patches for regolith sampling; artificial shadow tents at flow margins; restrict ops to low-sun hours to match polar lighting.
sites.key_differences: Weathered basalt with soil cover; desert shrubs; hot summers; no cold traps.
sites.name: Black Point Lava Flow
sites.why_analog: NASA's main 2008-2011 surface-ops analog; flat-to-gentle basalt plain fits landing-slope gates.

sites.experiments_done: Rover-instrument tests for Curiosity (CheMin, SAM) and ExoMars; carbonate globules like Martian meteorite ALH84001; contamination-control protocols.
sites.experiments_possible: Instrument cross-calibration on carbonate-basalt; sample-caching and cleanliness protocols; permafrost spring biology.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant pads for rover trials; clean-room tents for sampling.
sites.key_differences: Polar light regime; thick air; glaciers; Earth biology at springs.
sites.name: Bockfjord Volcanic Complex (AMASE)
sites.why_analog: ESA/NASA instrument-test site with Mars-meteorite-like carbonates in basalt.

sites.experiments_done: BoDEx 2005 field experiment on surface winds, dust concentration and radiative effects; deflation and yardang studies (Bristow et al. 2009); MODIS dust tracking.
sites.experiments_possible: Mars dust-lifting and saltation physics at the world's most active source: dust-devil and wind-gust lifting thresholds, dust-sensor and solar-panel cleaning tests, and electrostatic charging. Low-density diatomite (about 0.8 g/cm³) gives a direct test material for low-density Martian dust deposits. Yardangs in lake sediments are analogs for the Medusae Fossae Formation.
sites.how_to_modify: Deploy Mars-like solar arrays and dust sensors; CO2 low-pressure wind tunnel on site using local diatomite; basaltic dust plots for comparison.
sites.key_differences: Very hot; security makes access difficult; diatomite is biogenic silica, not basaltic dust.
sites.name: Bodele Depression (diatomite deflation basin)
sites.why_analog: Fills GSOP's new dust column (dust_index in the thermal-inertia family). It emits the most dust of any place on Earth, has a dust-scale thermal-inertia surface and is flat. It has not been used as a Mars analog; the nearest Mars site in the list (Emi Koussi, also new) is about 330 km away.

sites.experiments_done: Quaternary/permafrost studies (Schirrmeister et al. 2010); NASA Earth Observatory feature 2020.
sites.experiments_possible: Large flat unvegetated terrain for lander plume-surface interaction on fine grains in frozen ground; landing-zone LiDAR on featureless plains (a hard case for terrain-relative navigation); permafrost ice-content mapping with GPR; polar low-sun imaging.
sites.how_to_modify: Drop boulder fields and blast small craters to raise roughness/relief; basalt simulant pads.
sites.key_differences: Marine sand, flat (too smooth vs lunar relief); maritime humidity; storm flooding.
sites.name: Bunge Land (Zemlya Bunge)
sites.why_analog: A 6,200 km² barren sandy plain at 75°N with permafrost, unlike the vegetated tundra around it. It scores at the maximum on slope (0.30 weight) and high on cold-dry ground. It is ideal as a landing-zone stand-in, but its relief is weak.

sites.experiments_done: After Mariner 9 (1971-72) the Scablands became the type analog for Martian outflow channels (Baker & Milton 1974): streamlined islands, cataracts, giant current ripples.
sites.experiments_possible: Flood-bedform scaling to Mars gravity; drone DEMs vs HiRISE DTMs; rover traverse across cataract terrain; basalt-cliff stratigraphy.
sites.how_to_modify: Little modification needed; use cleared basalt benches for rover tests.
sites.key_differences: Farmland and shrub steppe; Earth gravity changes flow scaling.
sites.name: Channeled Scablands (Dry Falls)
sites.why_analog: The classic Mars outflow-channel analog.

sites.experiments_done: Remote sensing of salt crusts and seasonal flooding; no planetary work (nearby Chott el Gharsa appears in sabkha-life papers).
sites.experiments_possible: Analog for Martian chloride deposits and groundwater-fed evaporites; salt-polygon mapping; rover ops on crust; mirage optics for navigation-camera testing.
sites.how_to_modify: Dry-season plots; perchlorate spiking; covered evaporation pans.
sites.key_differences: Seasonal flooding; thick air; road crosses the playa.
sites.name: Chott el Djerid
sites.why_analog: A very large accessible playa (~7,000 km²) with no analog history; flat and evaporitic.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo 15-17 crews practised landmark recognition and traverses; Lunar Module mock-up landing-site location tests (Bailey 1967); Grover rover-simulator drives; USGS remote field-geology mission control trials.
sites.experiments_possible: Crater-counting and photogrammetry calibration; terrain-relative navigation datasets for landers; rover wheel-slip tests in loose cinder; Artemis LTV (lunar terrain vehicle) driving rehearsal; regolith-disturbance studies from rocket plume (small engine on a test stand).
sites.how_to_modify: Re-blast fresh craters to the LROC-mapped pattern of an Artemis landing zone; top-dress with fine (<100 micron) simulant; add boulder fields from local basalt to match lunar rock abundance.
sites.key_differences: Craters are explosive, not hypervelocity (no shock metamorphism); cinder is coarse and moist; mid-latitude lighting.
sites.name: Cinder Lake Crater Field
sites.why_analog: Only full-scale, purpose-built replica of a real lunar landing site; ideal for navigation and EVA rehearsal.

sites.experiments_done: ESA long-duration isolation, hypoxia and circadian studies; human-factors research for Moon/Mars bases.
sites.experiments_possible: Lunar-night analog human factors; closed-loop life-support tests; extreme-cold hardware tests.
sites.how_to_modify: Add regolith-filled test bins; shielded habitat berms of snow as regolith proxy.
sites.key_differences: No rock or regolith; ice plateau; air at 0.64 atm.
sites.name: Concordia Station (Dome C)
sites.why_analog: ESA's main human-isolation analog for lunar base living.

sites.experiments_done: NASA BASALT (2016) Mars EVA science-operations campaign on basalt flows; FINESSE volcanology and lava-tube work.
sites.experiments_possible: Basalt alteration sampling; EVA timeline tests with Mars comm delay; lava tube exploration.
sites.how_to_modify: Restrict to youngest flows (Blue Dragon); simulant plots; comm-delay ops.
sites.key_differences: Sagebrush on older flows; seasonal snow; thick air.
sites.name: Craters of the Moon (BASALT)
sites.why_analog: NASA's flagship Mars EVA-ops basalt site alongside Hawaii.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo 14 crew visited 1969; NASA SSERVI FINESSE team used it for lunar/Mars volcanic field science, LiDAR and handheld-instrument trials; lava-tube studies.
sites.experiments_possible: Lava-tube mapping for lunar skylight exploration; thermal-inertia measurements of flow textures; robotic cave mapping; EVA protocol testing.
sites.how_to_modify: Restrict test zones to young flows; add simulant in tube floors; dark-adapted lighting inside tubes.
sites.key_differences: Basalt is K- and Fe-rich (not mare-like); seasonal snow and soil; vegetation.
sites.name: Craters of the Moon National Monument
sites.why_analog: Mature NASA analog with flows, cones and lava tubes in one place.

sites.experiments_done: NASA astrobiology studies of stromatolites, microbial mats and gypsum dunes in a desert oasis.
sites.experiments_possible: Biosignature preservation in gypsum sands; microbial-mat lipid biomarkers; stromatolite growth rates.
sites.how_to_modify: None feasible (protected); laboratory replicas.
sites.key_differences: Wet pools; vegetation; protected reserve.
sites.name: Cuatro Cienegas
sites.why_analog: Astrobiology reference oasis for microbial biosignatures in an evaporitic desert.

sites.experiments_done: Polyextreme habitability studies (pH <0, hypersaline, >100 °C); salt, sulfur and iron mineralogy; limits-of-life debate (Europlanet 2010s).
sites.experiments_possible: Brine chemistry and biosignature preservation in salts; Raman of hydrated iron sulfates.
sites.how_to_modify: Shaded instrument plots on inactive salt terraces.
sites.key_differences: Extremely hot; thick air; below sea level.
sites.name: Dallol
sites.why_analog: The most extreme hydrothermal analog on Earth.

sites.experiments_done: Morphometric yardang studies (Ehsani & Quiel 2008; Mousavi 2015); TAR mega-ripple analog paper (Foroutan & Zimbelman 2016); comparison with Aeolis yardangs (2025); MODIS land-surface-temperature records.
sites.experiments_possible: Field-measured yardang erosion rates to date Medusae Fossae and Aeolis terrain; TAR migration measurements; rover navigation through yardang corridors; extreme-heat thermal-cycling tests of hardware (day-night swing).
sites.how_to_modify: Night-time-only operations for thermal tests; basaltic simulant on corridor floors; wind-sensor networks.
sites.key_differences: Extreme heat (Mars is cold); thick air; clays not basaltic.
sites.name: Dasht-e Lut - Kalut yardang field
sites.why_analog: One of Earth's largest mega-yardang and TAR fields, with high roughness and relief scores. Its use has been remote-sensing only, with no field operations, and it is more than 100 km from all known sites.

sites.experiments_done: Rover and instrument tests; maar tephra and evaporite (Badwater salt) studies; dust devils; Viking-era analog work.
sites.experiments_possible: Maar tephra stratigraphy; evaporite spectroscopy; rover autonomy on varied terrain.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant lanes on tephra; shaded plots for thermal tests.
sites.key_differences: Very hot summers; thick air; tourism; salts are terrestrial (Na-Ca) rather than Mars-like Mg-Fe sulfates.
sites.name: Death Valley - Ubehebe Crater and basin floor
sites.why_analog: Classic US desert analog with volcanic and evaporite terrain together.

sites.experiments_done: Four-week integrated Mars simulation: analog astronauts in suit simulators, rovers, drones, 16 experiments, with mission control in Innsbruck under time delay.
sites.experiments_possible: Field-laboratory procedures; dust exposure of suits and seals; geology traverse planning with 10-20 min latency; evaporite biosignature sampling.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant pads; shaded tents for thermal tests; CO2 dust chamber in camp.
sites.key_differences: Limestone not basalt; very hot; thick air.
sites.name: Dhofar desert (AMADEE-18)
sites.why_analog: Large integrated Mars field simulation in hyper-arid terrain.

sites.experiments_done: Deliquescence and brine-formation studies; water tracks compared with recurring slope lineae; chloride chemistry.
sites.experiments_possible: Brine-stability and deliquescence experiments; time-lapse monitoring of water tracks; salt hydrology modelling for RSL.
sites.how_to_modify: Instrumented salt-crust plots with controlled humidity; CO2 domes.
sites.key_differences: Liquid brine volume far larger than anything stable on Mars today; thick air.
sites.name: Don Juan Pond
sites.why_analog: Most saline natural water body; Mars brine analog.

sites.experiments_done: JPL drove Mars rover test vehicles, including the MSL 'Scarecrow' rover, on dune slopes to study slip, sinkage and embedding risk.
sites.experiments_possible: Wheel-sand interaction; dune-climbing limits; slip-prediction algorithms.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic sand test lanes; reduced-mass rovers to mimic Mars weight-on-wheel.
sites.key_differences: Quartz sand not basaltic; air density changes grain transport.
sites.name: Dumont Dunes
sites.why_analog: JPL's standard dune-mobility test site.

sites.experiments_done: Yardang fields studied as analogs for wind-eroded terrain at Zhurong's Utopia Planitia site and the Medusae Fossae Formation; Chinese aeolian research.
sites.experiments_possible: Yardang erosion rates; drone photogrammetry vs HiRISE; rover navigation between yardangs.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant on corridor floors; anemometer arrays for erosion rates.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; tourism; lacustrine silts not volcanic ash.
sites.name: Dunhuang Yardang National Geopark
sites.why_analog: Large accessible yardang field for aeolian Mars terrain.

sites.experiments_done: Opaline silica sinter with nodular 'cauliflower' textures compared with Spirit's Home Plate silica (Ruff & Farmer 2016); hydrothermal microbiology; sinter biosignature studies.
sites.experiments_possible: Silica sinter biosignature testing; Raman/IR of opal-A vs Spirit data; sinter-to-chert ageing studies; rover sampling of fragile sinter.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant pads beside inactive sinter; sealed sinter plots to study silica dehydration under low humidity.
sites.key_differences: Active geysers and hot water; thick air; tourism.
sites.name: El Tatio geyser field
sites.why_analog: The best analog for Spirit's Home Plate silica.

sites.experiments_done: Petrology of its two alkaline series (Gourgaud & Vincent 2004); orbital and astronaut-photo comparison with Elysium Mons; no ground-based Mars work.
sites.experiments_possible: Ground truth for the Elysium Mons comparison: caldera-wall stratigraphy, trona (sodium carbonate) evaporites in the Era Kohor crater as a volcanic-lake evaporite analog, fumarole and hot-spring alteration (Yi Yerra), and rover ops at 2,000-3,400 m.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant pads in caldera floor; low-pressure dust tests.
sites.key_differences: Water-carved furrows on flanks (Mars volcanoes lack them); remote, insecure access; thick air.
sites.name: Emi Koussi volcano (Tibesti)
sites.why_analog: A large hyper-arid shield volcano with evaporites inside its caldera. The Mars comparison has only ever been made from orbit, so field work would be new. It scores on composition, roughness and relief.

sites.experiments_done: Integrated month-long Mars simulation with suit simulators, rovers and remote mission control.
sites.experiments_possible: EVA ops on hamada; dune mobility; dust exposure; fossil-bed biosignature recognition training.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant pads; dust chamber in camp.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; hot; carbonate rocks.
sites.name: Erfoud / Merzouga (MARS2013)
sites.why_analog: Major Mars mission simulation in the Sahara margin.

sites.experiments_done: ESA CAVES (since 2011): international astronaut crews spend about a week underground practising team behaviour, cave mapping, science sampling and communication with a surface mission control.
sites.experiments_possible: Subsurface operations rehearsal for lunar lava tubes: 3D mapping, underground communications relays, crew decision-making in darkness, and sampling protocols.
sites.how_to_modify: Mostly a human-factors analog; no surface modification useful.
sites.key_differences: Limestone karst is unlike lunar lava tubes; humid.
sites.name: ESA CAVES site (Sa Grutta, Sardinia)
sites.why_analog: ESA's underground human-operations analog for lava-tube exploration.

sites.experiments_done: Rare-earth and trace-element comparisons with lunar anorthosites (1976); pink spinel matching Chandrayaan-1 M3 detections (JpGU 2025).
sites.experiments_possible: Highland composition ground-truth for orbital spectrometers (M3/LRO); lunar spinel-anorthosite sample-selection training; handheld Raman/LIBS calibration; drilling in plagioclase-rich rock; low-sun Arctic lighting tests.
sites.how_to_modify: Crush local anorthosite into highland simulant on site; cleared test pads.
sites.key_differences: Metamorphosed (amphibole-bearing) anorthosite; wet maritime climate.
sites.name: Fiskenaesset anorthosite complex (Qeqertarsuatsiaq)
sites.why_analog: Composition is the weakest Earth variable in GSOP (silica index, match-ability 0.4). This is one of the few places with bare, lunar-like anorthosite at high latitude, and it carries a lunar pink-spinel analog that has only just been reported. It is a complement to Mistastin.

sites.experiments_done: University of Aizu Hakoniwa project (2025) building lunar analog terrain inside the national Fukushima Robot Test Field for rover and construction-robot tests.
sites.experiments_possible: Rover autonomy on engineered lunar terrain; lunar construction robotics (excavation, berm building); teleoperation from a remote control room.
sites.how_to_modify: Already artificial: add fine simulant and polar-light rigs.
sites.key_differences: Small artificial bed on a coastal, humid, built-up site.
sites.name: Fukushima Robot Test Field lunar analog ('Moon/Mars Garden')
sites.why_analog: Newest Asian lunar test field, with engineered terrain and robotics infrastructure.

sites.experiments_done: Desert geomorphology and Shuttle-radar discovery of buried palaeo-drainages in the Western Desert; prehistoric rock-art surveys; Viking-era aeolian comparisons.
sites.experiments_possible: Analog for Martian valley networks cut into plateaux: drone-mapped dendritic wadis vs Warrego Valles, testing groundwater sapping vs runoff, and radar sounding of buried channels (like SHARAD/RIMFAX).
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant aprons; GPR test lines; drone LiDAR baselines.
sites.key_differences: Sandstone not basalt; very hot; remote.
sites.name: Gilf Kebir plateau and wadis
sites.why_analog: Dendritic valleys in one of the driest places on Earth, with strong relief and water-aridity scores. There has been no modern analog campaign. It is about 150 km from Kamil crater.

sites.experiments_done: Impact-structure research since the 1960s (shatter cones, central uplift); planetary geology field courses and astronaut-style training trips.
sites.experiments_possible: Central-peak geology training (analog for lunar central peaks); drone-photogrammetry vs LOLA; rover traverses in the ring valley.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant pads on the ring-valley floor; boulder seeding.
sites.key_differences: Sandstone target; deeply eroded; spinifex and mulga; hot.
sites.name: Gosses Bluff crater
sites.why_analog: Best-exposed eroded central uplift, an analog for lunar central-peak structure.

sites.experiments_done: First NASA astronaut geology field trip (March 1964): reading stratigraphy and recording field observations, the foundation for later lunar field geology.
sites.experiments_possible: Stratigraphic-reading training for crater-wall and rille exposures; long-baseline stereo mapping.
sites.how_to_modify: Little to gain physically; use as classroom for stratigraphy only.
sites.key_differences: Sedimentary rocks unlike the Moon; extreme relief; vegetation and water.
sites.name: Grand Canyon (South Rim and inner canyon)
sites.why_analog: Historic first astronaut training site (low physical similarity).

sites.experiments_done: Archaeological survey of the Umm Jirsan tube (2019-24; PLOS One 2024) showing 7,000+ years of human use; Saudi Geological Survey mapping of the 14,000 km² volcanic field.
sites.experiments_possible: Lunar lava-tube habitat analog in a hyper-arid, unvegetated setting (the tube is ~45 m wide, 12 m high); radiation/thermal stability logging inside tubes; skylight-entry robotics; basalt ISRU (sintering) on site.
sites.how_to_modify: Seal a tube segment for habitat-module tests; simulant floor; remove modern debris.
sites.key_differences: Hot; tube floors hold sand, clay and water after rains; Earth air.
sites.name: Harrat Khaybar and Umm Jirsan lava tube
sites.why_analog: One of the largest tube systems in a true desert, with 14,000 km² of bare basalt. The tube floor and walls are protected from weather and light much like lunar pits. It scores high on composition and terrain.

sites.experiments_done: HMP: lunar/Mars EVA, rover (Moon-1 Humvee), drilling and crew-ops trials; polar-desert impact geology; spacesuit tests.
sites.experiments_possible: Polar-lighting traverse planning; permafrost-in-breccia drilling (cold-trap ISRU rehearsal); pressurised-rover ops; comm latency.
sites.how_to_modify: Lay simulant on breccia patches; cover a permafrost pit with a cryo-shroud to imitate a cold trap.
sites.key_differences: Carbonate target rocks; summer is 24 h daylight but sun higher than lunar pole; Earth atmosphere.
sites.name: Haughton crater (Devon Island)
sites.why_analog: Best combination of impact crater + polar desert; long NASA history.

sites.experiments_done: Mars EVA and pressurised-rover traverses; impact-hydrothermal deposits; ground-ice studies; FMARS habitat crews; spacesuit and drill trials.
sites.experiments_possible: Search for impact-hydrothermal minerals as an analog for altered crater deposits; ice-in-breccia drilling; long rover traverses with comm delay.
sites.how_to_modify: Mars simulant patches; CO2 tents for low-pressure dust tests.
sites.key_differences: Carbonate target rocks; polar light regime; thick air.
sites.name: Haughton crater - HMP and FMARS
sites.why_analog: Longest-running Mars field program; impact crater in polar desert.

sites.experiments_done: Meteorite and crater-field studies since 1931; small-crater morphology and degradation used as reference for small lunar craters; impact-geology field trips.
sites.experiments_possible: Navigation through a dense small-crater cluster; crater-degradation measurement vs LRO small craters; meteorite-fragment detection with handheld magnetometers.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant cover on crater floors; boulder seeding to lunar statistics; drone-LiDAR baselines.
sites.key_differences: Small, eroded craters; hot desert; vegetation.
sites.name: Henbury craters
sites.why_analog: Rare multi-crater small-impact field; useful for crater-cluster hazard navigation.

sites.experiments_done: HI-SEAS missions (2013-2018: 4, 8 and 12-month Mars missions) studying crew cohesion, food, sleep and 20-min communication delays; later lunar and Mars campaigns.
sites.experiments_possible: Habitat ops; suited EVA on basalt; ISRU demonstrations; dust airlock trials; communication-delay operations.
sites.how_to_modify: Regolith (cinder) berms around the dome; dust-control airlock tests; Mars-sol scheduling.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; tropical high-altitude climate; Earth gravity.
sites.name: HI-SEAS habitat (Mauna Loa)
sites.why_analog: Longest NASA-funded Mars isolation missions, on barren basalt.

sites.experiments_done: HI-SEAS missions (2013-2018: 4, 8 and 12-month Mars missions) studying crew cohesion, food, sleep and 20-min communication delays; later lunar and Mars campaigns.
sites.experiments_possible: Habitat ops; suited EVA on basalt; ISRU demonstrations; dust airlock trials; communication-delay operations.
sites.how_to_modify: Regolith (cinder) berms around the dome; dust-control airlock tests; Mars-sol scheduling.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; tropical high-altitude climate; Earth gravity.
sites.name: HI-SEAS habitat (Mauna Loa)
sites.why_analog: Longest NASA-funded Mars isolation missions, on barren basalt.

sites.experiments_done: Rover-based sediment provenance and transport studies; fresh-basalt alteration; dust and sand.
sites.experiments_possible: Basaltic sand provenance (Jezero delta analog); rover navigation on fresh lava; weathering rates.
sites.how_to_modify: Little needed: barren fresh basalt. Add CO2 low-pressure tents for dust lifting and wind-erosion tests on sandur.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; glacial meltwater rivers; fresh basalt is unweathered compared to old Mars surfaces.
sites.name: Holuhraun lava field
sites.why_analog: Freshest basaltic flood lava and sandur on Earth.

sites.experiments_done: USGS Astrogeology (Shoemaker era) mapped maar-diatremes here and compared them with lunar craters, helping set criteria to separate volcanic from impact origins.
sites.experiments_possible: Crater-origin discrimination training (maar vs impact) for lunar geologists; diatreme stratigraphy; rover descent into eroded crater walls.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant patches on maar floors; boulder seeding to lunar rock-abundance statistics.
sites.key_differences: Volcanic origin; eroded; desert grassland.
sites.name: Hopi Buttes volcanic field
sites.why_analog: Historic comparison site for volcanic vs impact crater origin; good terrain scores.

sites.experiments_done: Chang'e-3/4 lander hovering, obstacle-recognition and hazard-avoidance tests over a field of artificial craters built to lunar statistics.
sites.experiments_possible: Terrain-relative navigation imaging; lander plume interaction with simulant; rover egress tests.
sites.how_to_modify: Refresh crater/rock distribution to LRO statistics of a south-polar site; lay fine simulant.
sites.key_differences: Small artificial patch; farmland; temperate climate.
sites.name: Huailai lunar landing test site
sites.why_analog: China's flight-qualifying lunar lander test field (details partly unpublished; coordinates approximate).

sites.experiments_done: Artificial craters dug to replicate the lunar south-polar landing site; lander sensor and hazard-avoidance tests from aircraft/helicopter.
sites.experiments_possible: Lander guidance tests; rover mobility on crushed anorthosite simulant; terrain-relative navigation datasets.
sites.how_to_modify: Top-dress with LSS anorthosite simulant (Sittampundi); add boulder fields from LRO statistics.
sites.key_differences: Hot, monsoon climate; granitic soils; small scale.
sites.name: ISRO Challakere lunar terrain test facility
sites.why_analog: India's flight-proven lunar landing test field.

sites.experiments_done: Soviet VNIITransmash ran Lunokhod wheel and chassis trials on Kamchatka volcanic terrain in the late 1960s before Lunokhod 1 (1970); recent volcanology of the 1975-76 and 2012-13 Tolbachik fissure eruptions.
sites.experiments_possible: Volcanic-plain rover trafficability; cold-climate tests; fumarole mineralogy.
sites.how_to_modify: Use the barren 2012-13 Tolbachik lava and scoria field; lay basaltic simulant over scoria for wheel-sinkage tests; winter campaigns for cold-start.
sites.key_differences: Wet, snowy; forest away from fresh flows.
sites.name: Kamchatka (Lunokhod chassis trials, Tolbachik area)
sites.why_analog: Heritage region of the first successful planetary rover; fresh basalt plains with high composition and roughness match.

sites.experiments_done: Impact geology and meteorite recovery (~800 kg iron fragments; Folco et al., Science 2010); GPR survey.
sites.experiments_possible: Ray-system mapping as an analog for fresh small lunar craters (rays are almost unique on Earth); ejecta-block distribution vs LROC small craters; landing-hazard detection on fresh small craters; regolith-gardening studies.
sites.how_to_modify: Spread basaltic simulant on part of the ray system to test spectral detection of fresh ejecta; add simulated boulders.
sites.key_differences: Tiny crater (45 m); sandstone target; hot; very remote.
sites.name: Kamil crater
sites.why_analog: One of the few craters on Earth that keeps a well-preserved ray system, which makes it a direct analog of the small fresh craters that dominate landing hazards at lunar sites. The hyper-arid setting keeps it pristine. It was found by satellite imagery, the way GSOP proposes to list candidate sites for review.

sites.experiments_done: Identified from space imagery (c. 1987); field studies 1987-91 (Gurov et al.) and 2011 (Bouley et al.) on breccias, shocked minerals and the impact-vs-rift debate.
sites.experiments_possible: Large complex-crater geology at ~4,000 m: low air pressure (~0.6 atm), cold permafrost ground and strong UV in one place; central-uplift traverses; rover cold-start and battery tests; low-pressure dust experiments.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant pads on rim terraces; shade fences for cold plots.
sites.key_differences: Metasedimentary/granitic target; lake; pasture use; impact origin still debated.
sites.name: Karakul impact structure (Pamir)
sites.why_analog: It combines a large impact crater with high-altitude cold-dry ground, so it scores better on GSOP's cold-dry and temperature terms than any lowland crater. It has no analog history, and the nearest known site (Ladakh) is about 750 km away.

sites.experiments_done: Mars ice-terrain simulation with suit simulators, rovers and ground-penetrating radar on glacier ice.
sites.experiments_possible: Ice-margin mobility; radar sounding of ice (SHARAD-like); suit thermal management in cold.
sites.how_to_modify: Debris-covered ice plots on moraines (closer to Mars lobate debris aprons).
sites.key_differences: Clean ice not dusty ground ice; snow; vegetated valleys below.
sites.name: Kaunertal Glacier (AMADEE-15)
sites.why_analog: Mars ice-terrain simulation (fails GSOP ice gate).

sites.experiments_done: Apollo crews trained on fresh basalt, collapse pits and fissures; NASA BASALT project (2016-17) on Ka'u flows for EVA science operations.
sites.experiments_possible: Fresh-basalt sampling ops; pit-crater descent (lunar pits); thermal IR of cooling flows; EVA-timeline rehearsal with science backroom.
sites.how_to_modify: Restrict to Ka'u desert; floodlit night EVAs; simulant cover on test lanes.
sites.key_differences: Wet tropical climate on windward side; active volcanism hazards; no cold traps.
sites.name: Kilauea caldera and Ka'u Desert
sites.why_analog: Apollo's most-used fresh-basalt training ground.

sites.experiments_done: NASA BASALT (2016-17) ran Mars EVA science operations with communication delay on Ka'u Desert basalt; fumarolic alteration sampling; earlier Apollo and Mars instrument tests.
sites.experiments_possible: Science-backroom operations under Mars latency; alteration-mineral (sulfate, opal) mapping; sample selection under delay.
sites.how_to_modify: Comm-delay and EVA timeline constraints are the main modification; simulant pads for drill tests.
sites.key_differences: Wet tropics nearby; thick air; vegetated margins.
sites.name: Kilauea Ka'u Desert (BASALT)
sites.why_analog: NASA's main Mars EVA science-operations analog on basalt.

sites.experiments_done: Astronaut geology traverses on a 2 km maar with layered tephra; xenolith (peridotite) sampling exercises; field-geology instruction for Artemis crews.
sites.experiments_possible: Crater-rim EVA ops similar to Shackleton-rim traverses; tephra stratigraphy for regolith-layer interpretation; sample-return protocol drills; rover descent/ascent on crater walls.
sites.how_to_modify: Lay a simulant apron on the floor for sample triage; floodlit night EVAs to imitate low-angle polar sun.
sites.key_differences: Maar (explosive volcanic) not impact; hot desert; mid-latitude sun.
sites.name: Kilbourne Hole and Potrillo Volcanic Field
sites.why_analog: Large accessible crater with clean stratigraphy; current astronaut-training site.

sites.experiments_done: Viable ancient bacteria and nematodes recovered from Pleistocene permafrost; studies on long-term survival relevant to Martian ice.
sites.experiments_possible: Ice-rich ground drilling; contamination-free sampling of ancient ice; long-term microbial survival; GPR of ground-ice wedges.
sites.how_to_modify: Use core samples in Mars chambers rather than field modification.
sites.key_differences: Tundra, forest and thermokarst lakes; wet summers; fails vegetation gate.
sites.name: Kolyma Lowland permafrost
sites.why_analog: Reference for life preservation in ground ice.

sites.experiments_done: Reported mobility, navigation and hazard-avoidance field tests of the Chang'e-3 Yutu rover prototype in the Kumtag desert near Dunhuang (2010s); Chinese aeolian research.
sites.experiments_possible: Long-range rover autonomy on mixed gravel and dunes; dust-ingress tests of mechanisms; solar-array dust accumulation; rover egress from a lander mock-up.
sites.how_to_modify: Lay basaltic simulant lanes; blast small craters for hazard detection; low-sun dusk operations to mimic polar lighting.
sites.key_differences: Rounded aeolian sand and gravel, hot summers, thick air; mid-latitude sun.
sites.name: Kumtag Desert (Yutu rover tests, Dunhuang)
sites.why_analog: Chinese desert rover test area with flat, barren terrain (reported use).

sites.experiments_done: Jarosite-bearing deposits in altered rocks of Kutch characterised as Mars analog (Bhattacharya et al. 2016); Indian Mars analog studies.
sites.experiments_possible: Spectroscopy vs CRISM jarosite; alteration pathways in basaltic-volcaniclastic rocks; Indian instrument tests.
sites.how_to_modify: Cleared plots on jarosite beds; dry-season ops.
sites.key_differences: Hot; monsoon rains; scrub and salt-marsh nearby (Rann).
sites.name: Kutch - Matanomadh jarosite
sites.why_analog: Accessible Indian jarosite (acid-sulfate) site.

sites.experiments_done: Mars analog characterisation: evaporites, borax and sulfur hydrothermal deposits, permafrost, high UV at ~0.57 atm.
sites.experiments_possible: Borate/sulfate spectroscopy (Gale borates); low-pressure, high-UV habitability; rover cold-start tests; ice-wedge polygon studies.
sites.how_to_modify: Shore plots; basaltic simulant pads; UV-sterilised plots.
sites.key_differences: Lake and grazing; thick air compared to Mars.
sites.name: Ladakh - Tso Kar and Puga
sites.why_analog: India's top Mars analog: evaporites, hydrothermal borax and sulfur, permafrost and high UV at 4,500 m in one area.

sites.experiments_done: Mineralogy and geochemistry of chimneys up to 60 m high, made of calcite and silica layers formed where hydrothermal fluids mix with lake water.
sites.experiments_possible: Analog for Martian mounds and spring deposits and for lake carbonates (Jezero marginal carbonates): imaging-spectrometer mapping of carbonate-silica layering, biosignature preservation in chimneys, and rover/drone mapping of tall vertical structures. Also a site for lake-retreat shoreline mapping.
sites.how_to_modify: Work on dry chimney fields away from the shore; cover active vents for clean sampling.
sites.key_differences: Very hot; active springs and a living lake (with flamingos); thick air.
sites.name: Lake Abbe hydrothermal carbonate chimneys
sites.why_analog: Rare on-land hydrothermal carbonate-silica chimneys in a desert, which raises its composition score. It has no analog use, and Dallol, the nearest known site, is about 380 km away.

sites.experiments_done: Acid (pH <3) saline lakes and groundwaters precipitating jarosite, hematite, gypsum and halite (Benison & co-workers) as analogs for Meridiani Planum sediments.
sites.experiments_possible: Acid-brine mineral precipitation; biosignature preservation in acid salts; rover spectroscopy of jarosite crusts.
sites.how_to_modify: Dry-season plots on salt crusts; covered evaporation pans.
sites.key_differences: Eucalypt woodland around; lakes ephemeral and wet; thick air.
sites.name: Lake Gilmore acid saline lakes
sites.why_analog: Living example of Meridiani-type acid-saline chemistry.

sites.experiments_done: ESA PANGAEA astronaut geology training (2016-); La Corona lava-tube exploration and mapping; Mars/Moon rover and instrument trials on the 1730-36 flows.
sites.experiments_possible: Lava-tube navigation; fresh-basalt sampling; astronaut-science team comms protocols.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant tracks on Timanfaya flows; sealed sections of La Corona for low-humidity and radiation logging; night EVAs under single low-angle light.
sites.key_differences: Ocean climate; tourism protections; mid-latitude light.
sites.name: Lanzarote - Timanfaya and La Corona lava tube
sites.why_analog: ESA's core lunar geology training area, combining fresh basalt and an accessible lava tube.

sites.experiments_done: ESA PANGAEA astronaut geology training; La Corona lava-tube exploration; Mars rover and instrument trials on fresh basalt.
sites.experiments_possible: Basalt-alteration sampling for Jezero-floor comparisons; lava-tube cave biology; sample-triage and caching rehearsal.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant tracks; night EVAs; sealed tube sections for low-humidity studies.
sites.key_differences: Humid ocean air; Earth biology in tubes; tourism.
sites.name: Lanzarote - Timanfaya
sites.why_analog: ESA training site with fresh barren basalt and lava tubes; scores high on composition and roughness.

sites.experiments_done: BRAILLE: robotic (CoSTAR/autonomy) lava-tube mapping, microbial mat sampling and life-detection instrument tests.
sites.experiments_possible: Autonomous rover/drones in tubes for lunar skylight exploration; radiation-shielding studies inside tubes; comms relay through skylights.
sites.how_to_modify: Seal a tube section for thermal-vacuum-lite experiments; scatter simulant at entrances.
sites.key_differences: Tubes are wetter and host microbes and ice; surface vegetated.
sites.name: Lava Beds National Monument
sites.why_analog: Densest accessible lava-tube cluster used by NASA for cave robotics.

sites.experiments_done: High-altitude diving and microbial ecology under intense UV and ~0.5 atm; lake sediment and volcanic-lake chemistry as an analog for Martian paleolakes.
sites.experiments_possible: UV-stress biology; volcanic-lake sediment biosignatures; low-pressure evaporation experiments at the shore.
sites.how_to_modify: Shore-based enclosures to lower pressure further; UV-lamp boosted plots.
sites.key_differences: Liquid lake (Mars lakes are ancient); slopes far steeper than landing gates.
sites.name: Licancabur volcano summit lake
sites.why_analog: Highest-altitude lake analog for ancient Mars lakes.

sites.experiments_done: Shocked basalt (maskelynite), impact-melt and post-impact alteration studies; comparisons with Martian craters in basalt; ISRO/PRL spectral work.
sites.experiments_possible: Impact-generated clays and carbonates in basalt; ejecta-alteration spectroscopy; crater-lake sediment cores as a paleolake analog (like Jezero).
sites.how_to_modify: Rim ejecta plots and dry-season shoreline cores only.
sites.key_differences: Lake, forest and farms (fails GSOP gates); humid monsoon.
sites.name: Lonar crater (Mars context)
sites.why_analog: Only simple crater in flood basalt; also a crater-lake analog.

sites.experiments_done: Shock studies in basalt (maskelynite), ejecta mapping, crater-morphology comparisons with lunar craters, ISRO/PRL spectral and geochemistry work since its impact confirmation in 1973.
sites.experiments_possible: Shocked-basalt sampling; ejecta blanket GPR; spectral comparisons with Chandrayaan data.
sites.how_to_modify: Use rim ejecta exposures; protected site limits modification.
sites.key_differences: Lake and vegetation; humid monsoon; weathered basalt.
sites.name: Lonar crater
sites.why_analog: Only well-preserved simple crater in basalt (lunar-mare-like target).

sites.experiments_done: Potash exploration and mining; palaeoclimate and salt-crust studies by Chinese teams; no planetary field campaign.
sites.experiments_possible: Analog for a Martian lake drying to salt (Gale, Columbus crater): ring-shoreline mapping, salt-crust volatile trapping, Mars-perchlorate interaction, and rover ops on hard salt crust.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant patches; crust gas-sampling chambers.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; potash works near part of basin.
sites.name: Lop Nur 'Great Ear' salt crust
sites.why_analog: A very large, flat and dry salt crust (top slope score) with clear shoreline rings. The nearest listed site (Kumtag, used for Yutu rover tests) is about 180 km away, so it passes the novelty rule, and it has had little analog use.

sites.experiments_done: Planetary-geology field courses and volcanic-morphology research on maars, cinder cones and basalt flows that resemble lunar dark-halo craters and domes; named for its lunar look in the 1860s.
sites.experiments_possible: Maar-rim operations; crater-origin training; thermal-inertia mapping of basalt vs cinder.
sites.how_to_modify: Seed boulder fields at Lunar Crater rim; simulant lanes across flows; floodlit night traverses for low-angle light.
sites.key_differences: Volcanic craters, not impacts; desert vegetation.
sites.name: Lunar Crater Volcanic Field
sites.why_analog: Lunar-looking basaltic field in the dry Great Basin.

sites.experiments_done: From 1968 Lunokhod drivers trained here to steer with slow-scan TV images and multi-second delays across artificial craters and boulders, before Lunokhod 1 and 2 (1970, 1973).
sites.experiments_possible: Historical only; tele-driving under delay could be repeated elsewhere.
sites.how_to_modify: Not recommended (inaccessible); recreate the concept (delayed-video driving yard) at an open desert site.
sites.key_differences: Small artificial yard in farmland; geopolitically inaccessible.
sites.name: Lunodrom (Simferopol-28, Crimea)
sites.why_analog: First purpose-built rover-driver training ground.

sites.experiments_done: Habitat simulations with crews; field geology across sandstone, basalt and gypsum; rover and drone tests.
sites.experiments_possible: Clay/gypsum sampling for alteration studies; drone-rover scouting; habitat ops with Mars-like comm delay.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant pads; low-pressure dust chamber on site; habitat module EVA lanes.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; hot; rocks are mainly sedimentary.
sites.name: Makhtesh Ramon (D-MARS, AMADEE-20)
sites.why_analog: Diverse geology (sandstone, basalt dykes, gypsum, clays) inside one crater-like basin.

sites.experiments_done: Opened April 2019: a nine-module Mars habitat on a 67 km² Gobi site with craters and caves; education and planned astronaut survival training.
sites.experiments_possible: Habitat operations; Gobi gravel trafficability for rovers; dust-storm exposure of seals and solar arrays; cave exploration protocols.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant pads; CO2 dust chamber.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; tourism focus; red beds not basaltic.
sites.name: Mars Base 1 (Jinchang)
sites.why_analog: China's dedicated Mars habitat analog.

sites.experiments_done: 300+ crew rotations: EVA protocols, habitat ops, geology and biology; mapping of sinuous ridges (inverted channels) like those on Mars.
sites.experiments_possible: Inverted-channel mapping; clay and gypsum sampling; human-factors studies; drone scouting for EVAs.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant patches for drill tests; CO2 tents for dust lifting; sol-based scheduling.
sites.key_differences: No basalt; thick air; vegetation patches.
sites.name: Mars Desert Research Station (Hanksville)
sites.why_analog: Most-used Mars human-operations analog, with inverted channels like Mars.

sites.experiments_done: ILEWG EuroMoonMars and other Moon-focused crew rotations since 2009: EVA protocols, habitat ops, lunar-instrument field tests, crew autonomy studies.
sites.experiments_possible: Lunar-base procedures with lunar-day/night scheduling; crew autonomy under delay; dust-management and airlock tests; geology EVAs with sample triage.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant patches for EVA sampling; 14-day 'lunar night' power-down scenarios; dust airlock trials.
sites.key_differences: Sedimentary rocks unlike the Moon; thick air.
sites.name: Mars Desert Research Station (lunar crews)
sites.why_analog: Widely used habitat analog with lunar rotations.

sites.experiments_done: 2008 and 2010 ISRU demonstrations (oxygen-from-regolith, excavation, RESOLVE drill) at Pu'u Hiwahine; 2012 RESOLVE volatile-prospecting rover test; PISCES lunar landing-pad paving (2015, Hilo).
sites.experiments_possible: Polar-volatile prospecting rehearsal on summit permafrost lenses; regolith excavation/oxygen extraction; basalt-paver landing pads; long-wavelength thermal mapping.
sites.how_to_modify: Bury cold traps (cryocooled bins) to test ice-prospecting drills; sinter local tephra into pads.
sites.key_differences: Hawaiian tholeiite and hawaiite are not lunar basalt; humid lower slopes; protected cultural landscape.
sites.name: Mauna Kea (PISCES / ISRU test sites)
sites.why_analog: Main ISRU field-demo site for lunar volatiles and regolith processing.

sites.experiments_done: Cold-desert soil and ice studies; rover and drill tests; polar-ops and isolation research by NASA and NSF teams.
sites.experiments_possible: Cold-trap ice prospecting with neutron spectrometers; extreme-cold battery/thermal tests; polar-night operations; rover autonomy in low sun.
sites.how_to_modify: Insulated shadow enclosures to approach cold-trap temps; simulant patches for regolith mechanics.
sites.key_differences: Sun climbs to ~36° in summer (lunar pole <2°); lakes and glaciers; air.
sites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Taylor/Wright valleys)
sites.why_analog: Coldest, driest ice-free ground on Earth; key cold-trap stand-in.

sites.experiments_done: Basaltic ash quarried near Merriam Crater to make JSC-1 and JSC-1A lunar mare simulants used in hundreds of excavation, drilling, sintering and dust tests worldwide.
sites.experiments_possible: In-situ excavation and bulldozing tests on the parent deposit; sintering/3D-printing landing pads from local ash; dust-mitigation coatings; geotechnical cone-penetrometer comparisons with Apollo data.
sites.how_to_modify: Crush and dry the ash to lunar grain-size distribution; add agglutinate-like glass by microwave sintering; test in vacuum tents.
sites.key_differences: Ash contains volcanic glass but is weathered and hydrated; grain shapes rounder than lunar agglutinates.
sites.name: Merriam Crater cinder deposits
sites.why_analog: Parent material of the most widely used lunar mare simulant.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo crew geology training on ejecta stratigraphy and inverted rim sequences; Shoemaker's crater-mechanics mapping used to read lunar craters; NASA Desert RATS suit and rover trials (late 1990s-2000s); shock-metamorphism studies (coesite, stishovite).
sites.experiments_possible: Artemis EVA traverse rehearsal on blocky ejecta; ground-penetrating radar of breccia lens; regolith-mechanics tests on fine rim debris; lander hazard-detection LiDAR on rim boulders; sample-triage drills (which clasts to bag).
sites.how_to_modify: Spread a few hectares of basaltic/anorthositic simulant on the rim to match regolith; use night-time ops with a single low-angle floodlight to mimic polar lighting; shade a crater-wall alcove with insulated covers to create a cold-trap test bay.
sites.key_differences: Target rocks are sandstone/limestone, not anorthosite or basalt; eroded and weathered; mid-latitude sun; no permafrost.
sites.name: Meteor Crater (Barringer)
sites.why_analog: Best-preserved simple impact crater on Earth and the classic Apollo training site; strong terrain match.

sites.experiments_done: Lunar highland analog work by LPI, Western University and CSA (2009-2011): sampling of anorthositic impact melt (Discovery Hill), melt-rock spectroscopy and astronaut-style field-geology traverses.
sites.experiments_possible: Highland-anorthosite melt sampling; spectral library for lunar highlands; drill tests in impact melt.
sites.how_to_modify: Use the anorthositic melt cliffs (Discovery Hill) as 2 km test window.
sites.key_differences: Lake fills centre; vegetation; subarctic wet climate.
sites.name: Mistastin (Kamestastin) Lake crater
sites.why_analog: Only accessible crater in lunar-like anorthosite.

sites.experiments_done: NASA 2008 Lunar Analog field tests: ATHLETE walking-rover, Chariot rover, habitat-module mobility and crew-ops trials.
sites.experiments_possible: Loose basaltic sand traction tests; regolith moving/berming for blast protection; lander mass-handling robotics.
sites.how_to_modify: Mix in angular crushed basalt; level a test pad for repeatable trafficability trials.
sites.key_differences: Rounded aeolian grains vs angular lunar regolith; humid; vegetation.
sites.name: Moses Lake Sand Dunes
sites.why_analog: Basaltic sand made it NASA's choice for heavy lunar mobility tests.

sites.experiments_done: Dante I (CMU/NASA, 1992) walking robot attempted to descend into the active crater to sample gases; early planetary walking-robot test.
sites.experiments_possible: Polar volcanic robotics; cold-start of mechanisms; fumarolic ice caves (lunar cold-trap-like microclimates).
sites.how_to_modify: Instrument the warm-ground fumarolic ice caves near the summit as natural 'cold-trap-next-to-heat' labs; add shade fences on summit plateau for low-sun lighting tests.
sites.key_differences: Active phonolite volcano; ice; extreme logistics.
sites.name: Mount Erebus (Dante I robot)
sites.why_analog: Polar, barren, and the site of one of the first planetary walking-robot field tests; very high cold-dry score but fails ice gate on flanks.

sites.experiments_done: Robotic seismic-network deployment and multi-robot lunar-mission demonstrations (rovers, drones, lander mock-up) on volcanic ash plains.
sites.experiments_possible: Multi-robot cooperative science; LOFAR-like antenna deployment; teleoperation from orbit-like latency.
sites.how_to_modify: Grade a landing zone on the summit ash plain; top-dress with fine basaltic simulant; set up a temporary relay mast to emulate a lunar comm satellite.
sites.key_differences: Active volcano hazards; snow; Earth gravity.
sites.name: Mount Etna summit area (ROBEX / ARCHES)
sites.why_analog: Europe's leading site for multi-robot lunar mission demos on barren basaltic ash, with long institutional experience.

sites.experiments_done: Only soil-biology sampling (southernmost known indigenous microbes) and a GPS station; no planetary campaign.
sites.experiments_possible: Low-sun illumination experiments on rock (Sun never rises above ~26°, lowest of any rock on Earth): solar-panel tracking, long-shadow navigation and terrain-relative imaging at grazing light; regolith (moraine) mechanics at 2,500-2,900 m in -40 °C; ice-adjacent volatile prospecting with neutron spectrometers at an ice/rock contact like a cold-trap edge.
sites.how_to_modify: Deploy shade fences to create artificial permanently shadowed patches on the moraine; spread anorthosite simulant on a cleared pad; use winter-season (polar night) runs to emulate lunar night survival.
sites.key_differences: Granite, not anorthosite; sun still 20x higher than at the lunar pole; access only by Twin Otter from South Pole (287 km).
sites.name: Mount Howe and the Scott Glacier moraines (southernmost rock)
sites.why_analog: Highest-latitude exposed rock on Earth, so it gives the best illumination match available (lunar target weight 0.18) plus the strongest cold-dry score (0.15). Terrain slope (15-23° measured on moraines) is moderate. No previous planetary use, and it lies more than 1,000 km from the Dry Valleys sites.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo crews trained here in 1965 and 1967 on fissure-fed basalt, spatter ramparts and rootless cones; later volcanology of the Krafla Fires (1724-29, 1975-84) eruptions used to interpret lunar rilles and fissures.
sites.experiments_possible: Fresh-lava traverses; geothermal-powered habitat concepts; fissure and graben mapping.
sites.how_to_modify: Restrict tests to the 1975-84 Krafla flows (bare); overlay basaltic simulant lanes; use geothermal heat to run thermal-cycling tests alongside cold ground.
sites.key_differences: Lakes and vegetation; rootless cones require water (not lunar).
sites.name: Myvatn and Krafla lava fields
sites.why_analog: Apollo training on young basaltic fissure flows.

sites.experiments_done: Acid-sulfate steam alteration of basalt (Namafjall/Hverir) studied as an analog for sulfate- and silica-rich hydrothermal terrains; Skutustadir rootless cones mapped as analogs of Martian rootless cones (lava over ground ice); Apollo-era training in the same district (1965/67).
sites.experiments_possible: Alteration-zone mapping with hyperspectral drones vs CRISM signatures; lava-ice interaction studies for Mars rootless cones; biosignature preservation in sulfate crusts; geothermal-power concepts for Mars bases.
sites.how_to_modify: Restrict to the Namafjall fumarole field and barren cone fields (2 km window); CO2 tents for sublimation and alteration-rate experiments.
sites.key_differences: Lake, wetlands and farmland; the cones need water, which on Mars was ground ice; thick air.
sites.name: Myvatn - Namafjall (hydrothermal + rootless cones)
sites.why_analog: Two Mars processes side by side: acid-steam alteration and lava-ice interaction.

sites.experiments_done: Dune dynamics and fog-moisture studies; Mars dune-field analog; salt-crust and gypsum studies; Gobabeb research station work.
sites.experiments_possible: Barchan migration monitoring vs Mars dunes; fog-humidity effects on salts (deliquescence analog); rover dune mobility.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic sand plots; humidity-controlled salt enclosures.
sites.key_differences: Fog makes it far wetter near the surface than Mars; quartz sand.
sites.name: Namib Desert (Gobabeb)
sites.why_analog: Large dune sea with a permanent research station.

sites.experiments_done: Iron-oxide (hematite) concretions in Navajo Sandstone used to interpret Opportunity's Meridiani 'blueberries' (Chan et al. 2004); diagenetic fluid-flow studies.
sites.experiments_possible: Concretion-forming groundwater chemistry; rover microscopic-imager and spectrometer tests on concretions; age dating of diagenesis.
sites.how_to_modify: Mix jarosite/sulfate sand with concretions in test beds to mimic Meridiani lag deposits.
sites.key_differences: Aeolian sandstone not sulfate-rich basaltic sand (Meridiani); thick air.
sites.name: Navajo Sandstone hematite concretions (Grand Staircase-Escalante)
sites.why_analog: Best analog for Meridiani hematite spherules.

sites.experiments_done: NASA NEEMO missions (2001-): saturation-diving crews simulate EVA under partial gravity by weighting, test sampling tools, telemedicine and communication delays.
sites.experiments_possible: Partial-gravity EVA techniques and tool use; long-duration confinement; telemedicine; communication-delay protocols for lunar surface ops.
sites.how_to_modify: Already engineered; adjust suit ballast to lunar gravity.
sites.key_differences: Underwater: no terrain, light or thermal analogy (fails water gate).
sites.name: NEEMO (Aquarius Reef Base)
sites.why_analog: Major EVA-ops analog but terrain gate fails (good validation case).

sites.experiments_done: Astronaut field training on caldera geology and pumice; lava-tube visits; instrument tests by NASA teams.
sites.experiments_possible: Lava-tube navigation and comms tests (Lava River Cave ~1.6 km); obsidian/pumice spectroscopy; caldera-wall ops.
sites.how_to_modify: Use only the Big Obsidian Flow and cave interior; tent off vegetation for imaging tests.
sites.key_differences: Forested; rhyolitic obsidian is not lunar; wet winters.
sites.name: Newberry Volcano - Big Obsidian Flow & Lava River Cave
sites.why_analog: Apollo-era volcanic training ground with an accessible lava tube.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo 14 crew sampled suevite and breccias; ESA PANGAEA astronaut geology training on impactites.
sites.experiments_possible: Impact-breccia recognition; handheld instrument tests on suevite; sample-return curation drills.
sites.how_to_modify: Use quarries (e.g., Aumuhle, Otting) as outdoor impactite labs; no landscape-scale modification possible in farmland and towns.
sites.key_differences: Heavily vegetated and built-up; temperate wet climate.
sites.name: Nordlinger Ries crater
sites.why_analog: Classic impact-breccia training site for Apollo and ESA astronauts.

sites.experiments_done: Ground-temperature monitoring from 4,200 to 6,893 m; ice-bearing ground thermal model; wind-snow studies; microbial mats in lakes.
sites.experiments_possible: Ice-bearing permafrost drilling at about 0.45 atm (closest Earth air density to Mars in this list); dust-devil ops in thin air; low-pressure ISRU water extraction; high-UV biosignature degradation.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant plots; UV-boosted chambers.
sites.key_differences: Steep volcanic slopes; still 50x Mars pressure; andesite.
sites.name: Ojos del Salado high-altitude permafrost
sites.why_analog: It has the best elevation/air-density score of any site, plus ground ice in a hyper-arid setting. It is emerging rather than popular, and is about 220 km from Pajonales.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo 15 crew practised sampling and describing crystalline rocks, preparing for the 'Genesis Rock' anorthosite search.
sites.experiments_possible: Highland-rock recognition training; handheld XRF/Raman calibration on anorthosite; sample-selection rehearsal.
sites.how_to_modify: Collect anorthosite blocks into a 'sample garden' on a flat bajada for repeatable training.
sites.key_differences: Mountainous and steep; mixed lithologies; hot desert.
sites.name: Orocopia Mountains
sites.why_analog: Apollo training site for highland (anorthosite) rocks.

sites.experiments_done: Smectite-rich Chinle Formation mudstones studied as spectral and stratigraphic analogs for Mawrth Vallis and other layered clay terrains; rover-instrument and remote-sensing calibration of clays.
sites.experiments_possible: VNIR/SWIR mapping of clay layers vs CRISM; rover sampling and drilling of swelling clays (wheel and drill sticking risk); organic preservation in clay-rich layers.
sites.how_to_modify: Lay basaltic simulant on clay surfaces to test dust-masking of clay spectra; dry-season tests only.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; layered terrestrial mudstones with fossils; national-park restrictions.
sites.name: Painted Desert / Petrified Forest
sites.why_analog: Best accessible layered smectite sequence in a dry setting.

sites.experiments_done: Hyper-arid soils with Mars-like oxidants and very low organics studied by Valdivia-Silva and others; Viking-type experiment comparisons.
sites.experiments_possible: Oxidant chemistry experiments; limits of detection for life-detection instruments; dust and UV degradation of organics.
sites.how_to_modify: Perchlorate-spiked plots; UV-sterilised strips.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; coastal fog influence.
sites.name: Pampas de La Joya
sites.why_analog: Atacama-like oxidant soils in Peru.

sites.experiments_done: Volcanology of the longest Quaternary lava flow on Earth; inflation structures and lava tunnels.
sites.experiments_possible: Lunar mare long-flow and sinuous-rille analog; lava-tube/inflation-pit exploration for lunar skylights; long rover traverses on a single basalt surface; regolith development on young basalt.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant lanes across the flow surface; seal a lava tunnel section for thermal/radiation logging; night-time cold-soak tests.
sites.key_differences: Basalt is alkaline, oxidised; air; vegetation patches.
sites.name: Payun Matru volcanic field and Pampas Onduladas flow
sites.why_analog: Has the longest Quaternary basalt flow on Earth, comparable to long lunar mare flows. It scores high on composition (basalt), roughness and slope, has no lunar analog history, and is far from other known sites.

sites.experiments_done: Danish Peary Land expeditions (1947-50) built Brønlundhus; archaeology of Independence I/II cultures; Quaternary geology. No planetary analog work.
sites.experiments_possible: Lunar-polar EVA rehearsal under 24-h low sun (spring/autumn sun stays within a few degrees of the horizon); long-shadow hazard detection; permafrost drilling as an ice-in-regolith analog; pressurised-rover traverses on unvegetated gravel plains; solar-power autonomy under circling sun.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant pads; shade tents to make permanently shadowed micro-plots; use spring weeks when sun stays below 10°.
sites.key_differences: Sedimentary rocks; snowfall; no vacuum; summer sun up to ~31°.
sites.name: Peary Land polar desert (central plateau)
sites.why_analog: Most northerly ice-free land (mostly north of 82°N) with only 25-200 mm/yr of precipitation, so it is a true polar desert. Illumination and cold-dry scores rank near the top of the list, and it is far from Haughton and Svalbard. It also gives a northern-hemisphere option to pair with Mount Howe.

sites.experiments_done: Earliest-life biosignature studies (stromatolites, hydrothermal cherts); Mars 2020 science team trained to recognise ancient microbial textures.
sites.experiments_possible: Ancient-biosignature recognition for Jezero sample selection; PIXL/SHERLOC-like instrument tests on cherts; sample-caching triage.
sites.how_to_modify: Cleared outcrop pads; contamination-controlled sampling tents.
sites.key_differences: Spinifex vegetation; hot; metamorphosed rocks.
sites.name: Pilbara - Dresser Formation stromatolites
sites.why_analog: Oldest well-preserved biosignatures on Earth.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo crews trained on maar craters (Elegante, MacDougal) and basalt flows; later desert ecology and volcanology studies.
sites.experiments_possible: Large-crater rim navigation; low-albedo basalt thermal tests; lander plume-surface interaction on fine dune sand nearby; dust-devil observations.
sites.how_to_modify: Use winter night ops; seed basalt simulant patches; shade tents for thermal-extreme tests.
sites.key_differences: Very hot; volcanic not impact; dunes and creosote shrubs.
sites.name: Pinacate and Gran Desierto (El Pinacate)
sites.why_analog: Apollo heritage site with world-class maar craters in a hyper-arid setting.

sites.experiments_done: Long used for remote-sensing calibration (thermal-inertia and radar) and rover field tests; desert varnish and basalt weathering studies.
sites.experiments_possible: Thermal-inertia ground truth for THEMIS-like data; rover autonomy across basalt-playa contacts; dust-devil and aeolian studies.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant pads on the playa; shaded thermal plots; corner-reflector arrays for radar calibration.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; military range access limits.
sites.name: Pisgah volcanic field / Lavic Lake
sites.why_analog: Mojave basalt flow with adjoining playa for calibration.

sites.experiments_done: Palagonitic tephra from this cone was used to make JSC Mars-1 simulant (1997), chosen for its spectral match to Mars bright regions; used in many rover-wheel, ISRU and plant-growth experiments.
sites.experiments_possible: Simulant production at source; spectral ground truth; ISRU water extraction from hydrated palagonite; dust-adhesion tests.
sites.how_to_modify: Dry and sieve tephra to Mars grain-size distribution; CO2 tents for dust-lifting tests.
sites.key_differences: Palagonite is hydrated and wetter than Mars; thick air.
sites.name: Pu'u Nene cinder cone (JSC Mars-1 source)
sites.why_analog: Source of the first widely used Mars soil simulant.

sites.experiments_done: Sulfate and chloride mineralogy; yardang classification compared with Medusae Fossae and Gale (Wang et al. 2018); Zhurong preparation; volatiles under salt crusts (2026).
sites.experiments_possible: Salt-crust gas trapping as a methane/volatile analog; yardang erosion monitoring; rover spectroscopy of hydrated sulfates.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic simulant pads beside sulfate crusts; sealed crust plots for gas sampling; CO2 low-pressure tents for salt-deliquescence experiments.
sites.key_differences: Thick air (0.7 atm at 2,700 m); terrestrial microbes; salts mixed with clastic sediment.
sites.name: Qaidam Basin - Dalangtan playa
sites.why_analog: China's main Mars analog with Mars-like salts.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo 15 crew trained on gorge-rim geology as a stand-in for Hadley Rille; layered basalt flows observed in walls.
sites.experiments_possible: Rille-rim traverse and descent-risk assessment; stereo-camera mapping of exposed basalt layers (lunar pit/rille walls); rappel-robot tests for lunar pits.
sites.how_to_modify: Add rope-access robotic test lanes to mimic lunar pit descents; clear and simulant-cover a rim strip.
sites.key_differences: Gorge is river-cut, not a collapsed lava channel; vegetation and soil; mid-latitude.
sites.name: Rio Grande Gorge (Taos)
sites.why_analog: Apollo-era rille analog with exposed basalt stack.

sites.experiments_done: MARTE drilled for subsurface acidophile life; jarosite and hematite similar to Meridiani Planum.
sites.experiments_possible: Iron-sulfate spectroscopy; subsurface biosphere drilling; biosignature preservation in iron oxides.
sites.how_to_modify: Dried-terrace test pads; drill-site enclosures.
sites.key_differences: Wet, vegetated; acid river still flowing.
sites.name: Rio Tinto (MARTE)
sites.why_analog: Best acid-sulfate (Meridiani) chemistry analog.

sites.experiments_done: Polyextreme habitability under high UV and freeze-thaw; gypsum domes and paleoterraces mapped as a climate-transition record (Hinman et al. 2022); drone and rover biosignature-search strategies.
sites.experiments_possible: Evaporite-hosted biosignature detection with drone-to-rover hand-off; sulfate spectral mapping vs CRISM; testing salt-related polygon formation vs freeze-thaw interpretations on Mars.
sites.how_to_modify: Exclude lagoons via 2 km window; UV-sterilised plots; basaltic simulant patches for contrast experiments.
sites.key_differences: Active lagoons (Mars evaporites are ancient); thick atmosphere; terrestrial life.
sites.name: Salar de Pajonales
sites.why_analog: High-altitude Ca-sulfate salar; one of the best early-Mars evaporite analogs.

sites.experiments_done: Halite crusts hosting endolithic microbes (deliquescence-fed) studied as analogs for Martian chloride deposits.
sites.experiments_possible: Chloride deposit biosignatures; deliquescence water budgets; rover spectroscopy of halite.
sites.how_to_modify: Covered plots on halite to study deliquescence under controlled humidity; perchlorate addition; basaltic dust overlays.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; coastal fog supplies moisture.
sites.name: Salar Grande
sites.why_analog: Analog for Martian chloride deposits and salt-hosted habitats.

sites.experiments_done: Oman Drilling Project cores; VSWIR imaging spectroscopy of serpentine, magnesite and dolomite veins described as analogous to Mars-orbit mineral associations that Mars 2020 explores; subsurface-biosphere studies in serpentinite.
sites.experiments_possible: Full Perseverance-style rehearsal: olivine-carbonate outcrop selection, abrasion and coring, PIXL/SHERLOC-type mapping, and caching. Testing whether orbital olivine-carbonate signatures separate serpentinisation from lake carbonates (a key Jezero question). H2/CH4 seep detection as a Mars methane analog. Sampling deep-subsurface life through existing boreholes.
sites.how_to_modify: Sterilised test outcrops (UV/ethanol) for contamination-controlled coring; basaltic simulant aprons around carbonate veins to mimic dust cover; CO2 tents for low-pressure abrasion tests.
sites.key_differences: Mantle peridotite is far more ultramafic than Jezero basalt; summer heat; thick air; active modern microbiology.
sites.name: Samail Ophiolite - Wadi Tayin massif
sites.why_analog: It has the highest composition score of any Mars site (0.23 weight). Olivine, serpentine and carbonate exposed together in a dry climate match the Jezero/Nili Fossae olivine-carbonate unit. Mineral studies exist, but it has never been used for field operations, and the nearest known analog field site (Dhofar, AMADEE-18) is about 550 km away.

sites.experiments_done: Indian and Russian station science; recent Mars-analog geomorphology (polygons, chloride lakes).
sites.experiments_possible: Lunar-base logistics rehearsal from an existing year-round station (India's Maitri); polar-night power and thermal survival tests; low-sun traverses; ice-free regolith excavation and berm-building; isolation studies with Indian crews.
sites.how_to_modify: Shade structures for cold-trap plots; simulant fields beside the station; light-tight huts for polar-night runs.
sites.key_differences: Gneiss bedrock; lakes; Lake Untersee (a known astrobiology analog) is only ~90 km away, which sits just inside GSOP's 100 km novelty rule.
sites.name: Schirmacher Oasis (near Maitri station)
sites.why_analog: It has an ice-free bedrock and regolith plateau, a full year-round station on site, and an Indian logistics route. It is the most practical polar test site for an ISRO-linked lunar-base rehearsal. Its terrain and cold-dry scores are strong.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo-era astronaut and USGS studies of ejecta blankets, rim overturn and crater shape from a known-energy explosion; calibration of crater-scaling laws used to interpret lunar craters.
sites.experiments_possible: Crater-scaling validation for lunar small craters; ejecta-block size statistics; seismic refraction of the breccia lens; drone photogrammetry vs LRO NAC comparison.
sites.how_to_modify: Use as a scaled model: overlay simulant on the rim; shoot small high-velocity projectiles into simulant beds next to it for side-by-side comparison.
sites.key_differences: Alluvium target, not regolith or basalt; explosion not hypervelocity impact; access restricted.
sites.name: Sedan Crater (Nevada National Security Site)
sites.why_analog: Largest known-energy man-made crater; unique calibration point for crater-scaling.

sites.experiments_done: Living stromatolite growth and microbial mat studies used to interpret ancient stromatolites.
sites.experiments_possible: Biosignature morphology; lipid biomarkers; imaging-spectrometer detection of mats.
sites.how_to_modify: None feasible (World Heritage, intertidal).
sites.key_differences: Marine and wet; not a terrain analog.
sites.name: Shark Bay - Hamelin Pool stromatolites
sites.why_analog: Living-stromatolite reference (fails water gate).

sites.experiments_done: Anorthosite quarried to make ISRO's lunar highland soil simulant (LSS) used for Chandrayaan-2/3 lander-leg and rover-wheel tests; petrology by GSI and universities.
sites.experiments_possible: Highland-composition reference spectra; simulant production; drill tests in anorthosite.
sites.how_to_modify: Quarry-floor test pads; crushed-rock simulant beds next to the source outcrop.
sites.key_differences: Vegetation and humidity; Archaean metamorphic rock, not lunar ferroan anorthosite.
sites.name: Sittampundi anorthosite complex
sites.why_analog: India's composition analog for lunar highlands.

sites.experiments_done: USGS drilled and tested the 'Explorer' geology vehicle on the extremely blocky SP flow (1965-67); Desert RATS habitat and rover traverses in the San Francisco Volcanic Field; NASA JETT Artemis EVA field tests in the volcanic field (2024).
sites.experiments_possible: Mobility testing over high-rock-abundance terrain (worst-case lunar boulder fields); lava-flow-margin science traverse; LiDAR/stereo hazard mapping; EVA suit abrasion tests on vesicular basalt.
sites.how_to_modify: Grade a flat pad on the flow apron as a landing-zone mock-up; scatter simulant over aa to fill voids like lunar regolith.
sites.key_differences: Steep cinder cone (≈30° slopes) exceeds lunar landing slopes; vesicular, oxidised basalt; vegetation on older surfaces.
sites.name: SP Crater and SP lava flow
sites.why_analog: Most boulder-rich accessible basalt flow in the US Southwest; heritage test site.

sites.experiments_done: Norite and anorthosite from the complex used as feedstock for the USGS/NASA NU-LHT lunar highland simulants (2008-); platinum-group mining and petrology.
sites.experiments_possible: Composition reference for highland spectra; simulant production; drilling and crushing tests in plagioclase-rich rock.
sites.how_to_modify: Use quarried rock in off-site test beds; no in-place modification (forest, mines).
sites.key_differences: Mountainous, forested mining district.
sites.name: Stillwater Complex
sites.why_analog: Source rock for NASA's highland simulant.

sites.experiments_done: Apollo crews studied shatter cones and impact breccias; mining-robotics and ISRU research since.
sites.experiments_possible: Breccia and shatter-cone recognition; deep-mine (SNOLAB) low-background radiation tests; mining automation for lunar ISRU.
sites.how_to_modify: Use bare outcrops of breccia and shatter cones and the SNOLAB deep mine as test sites; no surface modification possible in a city/forest landscape.
sites.key_differences: Deeply eroded; vegetated; norite not anorthosite.
sites.name: Sudbury Basin
sites.why_analog: Apollo-era large impact basin; good for impact-rock training though it fails vegetation/built-up gates.

sites.experiments_done: ExoMars rover-prototype navigation and Raman Laser Spectrometer field tests; volcanic-glass and alteration spectroscopy; Canary Islands Mars-analog training for planetary scientists.
sites.experiments_possible: Rover visual odometry on mixed lava and pumice; Raman/LIBS calibration on altered basalt; 2 m drill trials (ExoMars-type) in tephra; dust-devil monitoring on the caldera floor.
sites.how_to_modify: Temporary basaltic-simulant drill beds; CO2 low-pressure tents for dust lifting; night-time thermal-inertia runs.
sites.key_differences: Phonolite-rich (more silicic than Mars); thick air; national-park restrictions.
sites.name: Teide - Las Canadas caldera
sites.why_analog: ESA's main volcanic rover and instrument test ground.
