sites.experiments_done: Impact petrology of melt rocks and shocked gneiss (1960s-2000s); dating to ~1.6 Ma. No planetary analog work.
sites.experiments_possible: Rim-traverse EVA rehearsal on an unvegetated simple crater (a Shackleton-rim-style traverse at small scale); crater-wall rover descent; impact-melt sampling; thermal-inertia contrasts between rim and floor.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant pads on rim and floor; shade fences on the inner wall for thermal-cycling tests; drone LiDAR baselines.
sites.key_differences: Granite-gneiss target; hot Saharan climate; remote access.
sites.name: Tenoumer crater
sites.why_analog: A well-preserved, bare 1.9 km simple crater in hyper-arid desert. Its relief and roughness are close to small lunar craters, and it is far from known analog sites.

sites.experiments_done: Mg-sulfate (epsomite/hexahydrite) saline lake studied as an analog for Martian sulfate brines and evaporites.
sites.experiments_possible: Sulfate hydration-state cycling (epsomite-hexahydrite); microbial life in Mg-sulfate brines; spectral changes as salts dehydrate.
sites.how_to_modify: Dry-season playa plots; covered evaporation pans with controlled humidity.
sites.key_differences: Farmland; lake now largely dry/disturbed.
sites.name: Tirez Lake
sites.why_analog: European Mg-sulfate playa analog for Martian sulfate brines.

sites.experiments_done: ispace HAKUTO rover tests (2016-18, incl. night tests under side lighting); Bridgestone lunar tyre tests; SLAM navigation and in-crater communication tests on a 0.5 ha field with flat and 5-20° slope zones.
sites.experiments_possible: Rover traction on loose sand; crater-wall communications; navigation datasets.
sites.how_to_modify: Fine simulant beds; artificial craters; low-angle lighting rigs for polar-light tests.
sites.key_differences: Rounded humid quartz sand; coastal; temperate.
sites.name: Tottori Sand Dunes Lunar Demonstration Field ('Luna Terrace')
sites.why_analog: Japan's active lunar test field, with an established industry and university user base.

sites.experiments_done: Sedimentology and hydrology only (deflation basin, Late Pleistocene lake-to-sabkha history); oil-exploration traverses.
sites.experiments_possible: Analog for Martian chloride and sulfate deposits formed from upwelling groundwater (Meridiani, Terra Sirenum): mapping salt-polygon networks, testing groundwater-vs-runoff origin models, brine and biosignature sampling below the crust, and rover traction on deceptive crust over soft brine-mud (a mobility hazard analog like Spirit's embedding).
sites.how_to_modify: Instrumented crust plots with controlled evaporation; Mars-perchlorate spiking; drone-mapped polygon test grid for rover crust-breakthrough trials.
sites.key_differences: Very hot; shallow liquid brine (Mars evaporites are ancient and dry); dunes and alluvial fans add quartz/carbonate.
sites.name: Umm al Samim sabkha
sites.why_analog: About 3,000 km² of almost perfectly flat, barren evaporite (top slope score), fed by groundwater. That process is central to the debate over how Martian chloride deposits formed. No Mars analog literature was found for it. It also has an engineering use as a hazardous-crust mobility test.

sites.experiments_done: Astronauts studied fresh pyroclastic deposits and fumarole remnants as lunar surface analogs.
sites.experiments_possible: Fine pyroclastic regolith trafficability; cold-climate equipment tests; ash-deposit spectroscopy.
sites.how_to_modify: Use late-summer windows; lay basaltic simulant strips beside ash for comparison.
sites.key_differences: Silicic (dacite/rhyolite) ash, not lunar composition; wet and windy.
sites.name: Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes (Katmai)
sites.why_analog: Apollo-era site for fresh, unvegetated pyroclastic plains.

sites.experiments_done: Year-round physiology, hypoxia (3,488 m) and isolation research; proposed by Russian scientists (Demidov & Lukin) as a ground test bed for lunar and Martian base functions; Lake Vostok drilling.
sites.experiments_possible: Cryogenic-hardware cold soak at Earth's lowest natural temperature; isolation psychology.
sites.how_to_modify: Use as cold-chamber of last resort; all regolith must be imported.
sites.key_differences: Even 184 K is far warmer than lunar cold traps (<110 K, down to ~38 K).
sites.name: Vostok Station
sites.why_analog: Coldest natural temperature on Earth; sets the ledger limit for cold traps.

sites.experiments_done: Gypsum dune migration and mineralogy compared with Mars north-polar gypsum dunes (Olympia Undae).
sites.experiments_possible: Sulfate spectroscopy; dune migration with lidar; wheel tests on gypsum sand.
sites.how_to_modify: Basaltic sand test lanes beside gypsum dunes.
sites.key_differences: Thick air; missile range nearby.
sites.name: White Sands gypsum dunes
sites.why_analog: Mars north-polar gypsum-dune analog.

sites.experiments_done: Impact geology and meteorite studies since its aerial discovery in 1947; morphology comparisons of fresh simple craters.
sites.experiments_possible: Crater-wall rover descent; floor regolith trafficability; ejecta-rim LiDAR hazard mapping.
sites.how_to_modify: Simulant on crater floor; boulder seeding on rim; shade tents on the inner wall for thermal tests.
sites.key_differences: Laterite sandstone target, partly sand-filled floor, hot savanna climate.
sites.name: Wolfe Creek crater
sites.why_analog: Second-best preserved simple crater after Meteor Crater.

sites.experiments_done: Thermophile biosignatures in silica sinter; acid-sulfate alteration studies.
sites.experiments_possible: Silica sinter spectroscopy; biosignature preservation in sinter and acid-sulfate crusts; thermal-infrared mapping of hydrothermal ground.
sites.how_to_modify: None feasible (protected national park); use laboratory replicas of sinter.
sites.key_differences: Forested, wet, snowy; active thermal features are protected.
sites.name: Yellowstone - Norris Geyser Basin
sites.why_analog: Reference site for hydrothermal silica and acid-sulfate alteration.
